1. The publicly available data from the COMPUSTAT Fundamentals Annual database and the Audit

       etary PCAOB data were obtained through the PCAOB’s academic research fellowship program.
       In the research fellowship program, the author obtained access, collected the PCAOB data, and
       performed all the data analysis. The author has provided a letter from the PCAOB vouching for
       data access.

evidence.description: The PCAOB data require approved access and are housed on PCAOB IT equipment.
evidence.quote:
2. The proprietary data were obtained from the PCAOB after receiving approval from the PCAOB’s
       Board authorizing data access for a research proposal to provide evidence on auditors' use of
       shared services centers (SSCs). The data are housed and stored at the PCAOB and accessible only
       via PCAOB information technology equipment. As a condition for accessing the data, the
       PCAOB reviews the research to approve the release of any new nonpublic information. However,
       the author had academic freedom concerning the research design, interpretation of findings, and
       conclusions.

evidence.description: The datasheet describes PCAOB AFR source data, firm/year combination, and combination with Audit Analytics and Compustat; exact files and joins are not supplied.
evidence.quote:
II. Data sources
       The source for the data underlying the process of determining the use of shared services center
personnel is PCAOB AFR (annual firm review) documents for each of the Big 4 for the inspection
years noted in the study. The non-public annual firm review documents originate with the audit firms.
The PCAOB obtains, reviews, and uses the data for various purposes, such as planning the
engagements for review during their inspections. The audit firms complete the documents, which
include numerous data elements covering various aspects of the audit engagement (e.g., fee
information, audit hours information, engagement partner information, engagement quality review
partner information), and send the completed document to the PCAOB before the start of the inspection
year. I relied on the PCAOB-processed and PCAOB-checked data while also performing the additional
processing steps described below to determine whether an audit engagement involved the use of
offshore shared services center personnel and, if so, to what extent.
       I first combined the firm-provided data from each Big 4 firm for each inspection year in my
sample to create a dataset with the information for all Big 4 audit clients during my sample. I then
combined the PCAOB annual firm review data with Audit Analytics and Compustat data extracted
from Wharton Research Data Services (WRDS) to calculate other dependent and independent variables
necessary for my analysis. The engagement partner’s tenure on the client, the engagement quality
review partner’s tenure on the client, the engagement partner’s experience, if the engagement
underwent an unexpected engagement partner change, the count of the engagement partner’s other
audit engagements were provided directly by the PCAOB in the form it was used for analysis in this
paper, and I did not make any adjustments to the data provided. The indicator variable representing

evidence.description: The document states selected calculations and points to Appendix B for variable definitions.
evidence.quote:
whether the audit partner and the engagement quality review partner are in different offices was
computed by comparing the office data for each engagement partner and quality review partner
provided by the PCAOB. If the offices differed, the variable was coded as 1; if they were the same, it
was coded as zero. The audit hours, hourly audit engagement bill rate, and raw realization rate data
were provided directly by the PCAOB in the form used for analysis in this paper, and I did not make
any adjustments. The normalized realization rate data was the raw realization rate standardized and
zero-centered by audit firm and year. Appendix A of this file provides the source data for each variable.
Appendix B of the published manuscript provides the calculation definition for each variable.

evidence.description: The author defines SSC use from offshore-hours elements and says SSC hours and percentages were provided by PCAOB in analysis form.
evidence.quote:
I began with the PCAOB-processed annual firm review data for each Big 4 firm for the inspection
years within my sample period. The indicator variable for SSC usage is set to 1 for audit engagements
having one or more hours reported in the offshore shared services center hours data elements, and zero
for all other observations. The shared services center hours and the percentage of the audit performed
by shared services center personnel were provided directly by the PCAOB in the form used for analysis
in this paper; I did not make any adjustments to the source data.

evidence.description: The author describes PCAOB inspection findings as the Part I source and limits classification to reviewed engagements.
evidence.quote:
The PCAOB non-public inspection findings dataset contains information on each inspection finding
(i.e., each instance, which is described in the PCAOB’s inspection report of an auditing firm, where
PCAOB inspectors determined the audit firm did not comply with one or more auditing standards). For
each reviewed engagement as part of a PCAOB inspection, the inspection findings dataset indicates if
an inspection finding occurred. For the subset of engagements that were reviewed as part of the
inspection process, I classify the Part I findings indicatory variable as fir engagement that received a
Part 1 finding, per the Part 1 findings database, and a zero for each engagement that did not receive a
Part 1 finding, per the Part 1 findings database.

review_notes: The full supplied data-description text was read after screening its connected-block masking. It documents an empirical data construction and analysis target, but no separate analytical/theory model, numerical calibration, embedded author program, or standalone executable manual workflow. The author says PCAOB retains the proprietary conversion/analysis programs and logs; no executable or manual substitute is in this package.

The author names PCAOB AFR and nonpublic inspection findings as required sources; bounded local catalog queries did not identify those exact proprietary inputs. Their fellowship/permission and PCAOB IT restrictions remain an access barrier. The official public Form AP and SEC EDGAR routes do not supply the full unpublished PCAOB engagement inputs.

The author names Compustat and Audit Analytics products. Official product evidence indicates commercial/licensed access. Frozen metadata contains unverified candidates, including COMP.FUNDA and Audit Analytics fee, revised-opinion, restatement and internal-control records. Only candidate metadata was inspected; no dataset payload or rows were read.

The data sheet's Appendix A target variables were represented separately by source role: Compustat, PCAOB AFR, PCAOB inspection findings, Audit Analytics opinions, restatements, fees, controls, engagement characteristics, Form AP and Form 10-K. Exact raw fields, periods, joins, formulas and producer/consumer order remain incomplete.

SEC filing corpora paths are supported by exact workspace documentation. Stage One 10-X parsing documentation says tables are excluded. All filing/corpus paths remain unverified for the author's required client data and PRT_CLT_DIST construction.

No software requirement is specified in the author material. No author code, imports, compiles, model runs, statistical trials, or dataset payload reads were performed. Execution readiness and data-route resolution remain for the pinned finalizer to compute.
